methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Mind Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by RJ Scaringe, is evaluated against a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable. The private peer set includes Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics, alongside broader sector participants such as Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Two valuation methods are applicable to this stage and sector. The stage-progression method, anchoring to the company's $1.0B total capital raised proxy and applying a standard 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $2.0B. The peer-median approach uses a filtered set of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B, ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

Triangulating these two methods yields a valuation range of $1.4B to $2.3B, with a median of $1.9B. The peer-median result of $1.7B falls at the lower end of the range, reflecting the presence of one earlier-stage peer (Walden at Seed) that moderates the median. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the peer sample given stage dispersion (Seed through Series B) and the appropriateness of applying a uniform 2.0x multiplier without visibility into unit economics or growth trajectory. The $1.9B median represents the most defensible central estimate absent company-specific operational data.
